issues.title: Scaffold repository tooling
issues.body:
## User story

As a contributor, I want the repository rules, hooks and CI in place so that every change runs through an issue, a branch, the full test gate and a pull request.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `.claude/settings.json`, `hooks/issue-context.sh`, `hooks/branch-guard.sh` and its test suite are in place and pass
- [ ] `.claude/skills/gh/SKILL.md` describes the issue, branch and PR workflow for this repo
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` covers containers only (Makefile, Go 1.26), issue branches, four test layers, `make openapi`, no mocks below the layer under test, and style rules
- [ ] `run-tests.sh` is the single gate: shell tests, Go format/vet/unit, OpenAPI drift, web lint/types/vitest, compose-backed integration and Playwright on ports derived per worktree
- [ ] `release.sh` and its tests are ported; `CHANGELOG.md` follows Keep a Changelog
- [ ] `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `./run-tests.sh`; issue templates and a PR template with `Closes #` exist
- [ ] `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/decisions.md` record the architecture and the decisions taken so far
- [ ] `NOTICE` credits the Apache-2.0 code adapted from Armature

## Tests

`.claude/hooks/tests/branch-guard-test.sh` and `tests/test-release.sh` run inside `run-tests.sh` and in CI.

issues.title: Backend skeleton: config, database, migrations, HTTP route table
issues.body:
## User story

As a developer, I want a Go service skeleton that mirrors Armature so that every later feature plugs into the same patterns.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `backend/cmd/{api,worker,migrate,seed,openapi}` build
- [ ] Configuration from `STATOR_*` environment variables only, with validation and sentence-style errors
- [ ] `internal/db` cluster with primary/replica transactions and org row-level security via `current_org_id()`; IDs from `uuidv7()`
- [ ] goose migrations embedded and applied by `cmd/migrate`; `org` and `app_user` tables exist with RLS policies
- [ ] chi router with middleware chain (request id, metrics, logging, recovery, security headers, same-site check, timeout, authenticate) and a single error envelope
- [ ] The route table generates `api/openapi.json`; a unit test fails when the committed spec is stale and when router and table disagree
- [ ] `/healthz`, `/readyz` and `/metrics` respond

## Tests

Unit tests for config and route table; integration test proving RLS isolates two orgs even through raw SQL.

issues.title: Web skeleton: routing, API client, app shell
issues.body:
## User story

As a user, I want a fast single-page app with a clear shell (rail, sidebar, content) so that navigating the wiki feels like Armature.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] React 19, TypeScript, Vite, TanStack Router and Query
- [ ] openapi-fetch client typed from `web/src/api/schema.d.ts` generated from `api/openapi.json`
- [ ] Shell with rail, collapsible sidebar, top bar with search entry point and user menu
- [ ] Error and empty states follow Armature's design docs; user-facing constants live in `web/src/config.ts`
- [ ] ESLint, `tsc --noEmit` and vitest wired into `run-tests.sh`

## Tests

Vitest for shell components; Playwright smoke test loads the app and navigates.

issues.title: Compose stack and Makefile with containerised toolchains
issues.body:
## User story

As a developer, I want `make up` to start the complete stack and every toolchain to run in a container so that nothing has to be installed on the host.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `deploy/docker-compose.yml` with postgres, valkey, seaweedfs, mailpit, keycloak (realm with clients for Stator and Armature), migrate, seed, api, worker, web and armature-stub
- [ ] Dockerfiles for backend and web; nginx config for the web image
- [ ] Makefile targets: up, down, clean, logs, seed, test, test-integration, test-e2e (ONLY=, WORKERS=), test-all, openapi, vet, fmt, npm ARGS=, web-build, shell
- [ ] Go 1.26 and Node run as containers with caches under `.cache/`
- [ ] Compose project name and host ports derive from the worktree path so parallel worktrees do not collide

## Tests

`run-tests.sh` brings the stack up and down; CI proves it on a clean runner.

issues.title: Single sign-on via OIDC with sessions and group sync
issues.body:
## User story

As an organisation admin, I want members to log in through our identity provider and have their groups follow them so that access is managed in one place.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One OIDC provider per organisation (issuer, client id, secret, scopes, groups claim, enabled), configurable by admins
- [ ] Login via `/auth/oidc/{orgSlug}/start` and `/auth/oidc/callback`; users are created or updated by subject
- [ ] Groups from the groups claim are synced into Stator groups
- [ ] Sessions in an HttpOnly cookie; only the SHA-256 of the token is stored; logout and expiry work
- [ ] Backchannel issuer rewrite for in-cluster access, as in Armature
- [ ] Optional local password login for bootstrap admins (argon2)

## Tests

Unit tests for claim mapping; integration tests against Keycloak in compose; Playwright login fixture used by all e2e tests.

issues.title: Themes: design tokens, light/dark, custom themes, import
issues.body:
## User story

As a user, I want Stator to look and feel exactly like Armature, including my custom themes, so that both tools read as one product.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tailwind v4 `@theme` tokens identical to Armature's Clay light and dark values
- [ ] Light / dark / system switch stored per browser and applied before first paint
- [ ] Server-stored custom themes with the same spec as Armature (colors, fonts, shape, shadows, cursors, icons, backdrop, effect, css) and the same limits
- [ ] Built-in Deep-Tech and Constellation themes; organisation default theme
- [ ] Import and export in the `armature-theme/1` format, so Armature theme files work unchanged
- [ ] Theme editor with live preview

## Tests

Vitest: token list matches the stylesheet, compiler output; integration: theme CRUD and import; Playwright: switch themes and import `minecraft.armature-theme.json`.

issues.title: Playwright end-to-end harness
issues.body:
## User story

As a developer, I want a Playwright suite running against the real compose stack so that every user flow is proven in a browser before it is pushed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `e2e/` Playwright project with TypeScript, base URL from the per-worktree ports
- [ ] Fixtures: logged-in user via Keycloak, fresh organisation per test file, seeded data helpers through the API
- [ ] Traces and screenshots on failure, uploaded as CI artifacts
- [ ] Runs from `run-tests.sh` and `make test-e2e` with `ONLY=` and `WORKERS=`

## Tests

The harness proves itself with a login smoke test.

issues.title: Responsive layout and accessibility baseline
issues.body:
## User story

As a user on a phone or with assistive technology, I want every screen to be usable so that nobody is locked out of the documentation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Layouts work from 360px wide upwards; sidebar becomes a drawer on small screens
- [ ] Keyboard navigation for all interactive elements, visible focus ring, skip link
- [ ] Landmarks, labels and ARIA roles on shell, tree and editor toolbar
- [ ] Automated axe checks in Playwright on the main screens

## Tests

Playwright with @axe-core/playwright on shell, page view, editor and search; mobile viewport run.

issues.title: Spaces with home page and space settings
issues.body:
## User story

As a team, I want our own space with a home page so that our documentation has a clear place and entry point.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Create, rename, describe and delete spaces; each space has a unique key and a home page
- [ ] Space directory listing all spaces the user can see
- [ ] Space settings for admins: details, permissions, trash
- [ ] Space key appears in URLs: `/s/{spaceKey}/...`

## Tests

Unit: key validation; integration: CRUD and RLS; Playwright: create a space and land on its home page.

issues.title: Page tree with drag-and-drop, move and copy
issues.body:
## User story

As an author, I want to arrange pages in a nested tree so that readers find related content together.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pages have a parent and a rank; unlimited nesting
- [ ] Sidebar tree with lazy loading, expand/collapse and keyboard support
- [ ] Drag and drop to reorder or re-parent; cycles are refused
- [ ] Move and copy a page with or without its children, also into another space
- [ ] Breadcrumbs on every page

## Tests

Unit: rank maths; integration: move/copy including subtree and permission checks; Playwright: drag a page under another.

issues.title: Trash and restore
issues.body:
## User story

As an author, I want deleted pages to go to a trash so that mistakes can be undone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Deleting a page moves it and its children to the space trash
- [ ] Restore puts the page back at its former position or under the space home if the parent is gone
- [ ] Space admins can purge single items or empty the trash
- [ ] Trashed pages are excluded from tree, search and macros

## Tests

Integration: delete/restore/purge; Playwright: delete and restore a page.

issues.title: Rich-text editor: formatting, slash menu, tables, code, panels, anchors
issues.body:
## User story

As an author, I want a fast editor with the building blocks of technical documentation so that writing feels natural.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] TipTap 3 editor reusing Armature's editor components
- [ ] Headings, bold, italic, strike, code, links, lists, task-style checklists, quotes, horizontal rule
- [ ] Markdown-style shortcuts as you type and on paste
- [ ] Slash menu listing every insertable block, filterable by typing
- [ ] Tables with header row/column, add/remove rows and columns, merge cells, cell background
- [ ] Code blocks with language picker and syntax highlighting
- [ ] Panels: info, note, success, warning, error
- [ ] Every heading gets a stable anchor; copying a heading link works
- [ ] Server validates documents against a node and mark allowlist

## Tests

Unit (Go): document validation; vitest: extensions; Playwright: slash menu, table, code block, panel, heading link.

issues.title: Drafts and publishing with version comment
issues.body:
## User story

As an author, I want to work on a draft and publish when ready so that readers only see finished content.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Edits autosave to a private draft per page
- [ ] Publish creates a new version with an optional comment and an option to notify watchers
- [ ] Unpublished new pages are visible only to their creator
- [ ] Discard draft reverts to the published version
- [ ] Conflict detection when another person published in between

## Tests

Integration: draft/publish lifecycle and conflicts; Playwright: edit, autosave, publish with comment.

issues.title: Full-text search with filters and quick search
issues.body:
## User story

As a reader, I want to find any page quickly so that I do not have to know where something lives.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] PostgreSQL full-text search over titles, bodies and comments, ranked, with highlighted snippets
- [ ] Filters: space, author, last modified, label, content type

Integration: ranking, filters and permission trimming; Playwright: quick search and filtered search.

issues.title: Permissions: global, space and page restrictions
issues.body:
## User story

As an admin, I want to control who can see and edit which content so that sensitive documentation stays protected.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Global permissions: use Stator, create spaces, administer
- [ ] Space permissions per user and group: view, add pages, add comments, delete, administer
- [ ] Page restrictions for view and edit, inherited by child pages
- [ ] Enforced in the service and in the database; attempts through raw SQL are refused as well
- [ ] UI shows why a page is restricted and who can access it

## Tests

Integration: permission matrix including a raw-SQL attempt; Playwright: restricted page is hidden from another user.

issues.title: Attachments
issues.body:
## User story

As an author, I want to attach files and images by dragging or pasting so that pages can carry screenshots and documents.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Upload via drag-and-drop, paste and file picker; stored in S3-compatible storage
- [ ] Images render inline with resize and alt text

## Tests

Integration: upload/download against SeaweedFS and permission checks; Playwright: paste an image.

issues.title: REST API with OpenAPI and personal access tokens
issues.body:
## User story

As an integrator, I want a documented API and personal tokens so that scripts and other tools can read and write content.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All UI operations are available under `/api/v1` and described in `api/openapi.json`, served at `/api/v1/openapi.json`
- [ ] Personal access tokens with prefix, optional expiry and optional read-only scope; only hashes stored
- [ ] Token management UI

## Tests

Integration: every response is validated against the spec and the suite fails if an operation is not exercised; Playwright: create and revoke a token.

issues.title: Page comments

issues.title: Inline comments
issues.body:

issues.title: Mentions

issues.title: In-app and email notifications
issues.body:
## User story

As a user, I want to be notified in the app and by email so that I never miss a mention or an important change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Notification centre with unread badge, mark read, mark all read

issues.title: Connect an Armature instance
issues.body:
## User story

As an admin and as a user, I want to connect Stator to Armature so that pages can show and create issues with my own rights.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Org admins set the Armature base URL
- [ ] Each user stores their Armature personal access token under Profile; encrypted at rest with `STATOR_SECRET_KEY`
- [ ] Every Armature call is made as the viewing user through the SSRF guard; no shared bot token for reads
- [ ] Clear message and connect button when a user has not connected yet
- [ ] `cmd/armature-stub` implements the Armature API subset used; a contract test checks it against Armature's `api/openapi.json`

## Tests

Unit: token encryption; integration: proxy against the stub; Playwright: connect flow.

issues.title: Smart links for Armature issues
issues.body:
## User story

As an author, I want Armature issue keys and URLs to turn into live chips so that readers see status at a glance.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pasting an Armature issue URL or typing a known issue key converts it to a chip
- [ ] Chip shows key, summary, type icon and status, with a hover card
- [ ] Readers without access see only the key

## Tests

Vitest: key detection; Playwright: paste a URL against the stub.

issues.title: Armature issue block
issues.body:

As an author, I want to embed a single Armature issue with live details so that specs and work stay in sync.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Insert via slash menu by key or URL
- [ ] Shows summary, status, assignee, priority; refreshes on view
- [ ] Cached per user in Valkey for a short time

## Tests

Integration: proxy and cache; Playwright: insert and render the block.

issues.title: Armature issue list block from a query
issues.body:

As an author, I want to embed a live table of Armature issues from a query so that status pages build themselves.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Insert with an NQL query, chosen columns and maximum rows
- [ ] Renders as a sortable table with total count and a link to the full result in Armature
- [ ] Query errors are shown as sentences that say how to fix them

## Tests

Integration: search proxy; Playwright: insert a list and see rows.

issues.title: Create Armature issues from selected text
issues.body:
## User story

As an author, I want to turn selected text into Armature issues so that action items from a document become tracked work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Selecting text offers Create issue; choose project and type, summary prefilled
- [ ] Multiple issues from a table or list selection, one per row or item

## Tests

Integration: create proxy; Playwright: create an issue from a selection against the stub.

issues.title: Show pages that mention an issue in Armature
issues.body:
## User story

As an Armature user, I want to see which documentation pages reference an issue so that I can jump to the spec.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On publish, Stator extracts issue keys and syncs remote links in Armature (add and remove)
- [ ] Requires the remote links feature in Armature (issue filed in Cloudster1/Armature)
- [ ] Failures are retried through the outbox

## Tests

Integration: sync against the stub; manual check against a local Armature.

issues.title: Receive Armature webhooks to refresh cached issues
issues.body:
## User story

As a reader, I want issue chips and blocks to reflect changes promptly so that pages never show stale status.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `/api/v1/armature/webhook` verifies `X-Armature-Signature-256` with a per-org secret
- [ ] issue.updated, issue.transitioned and comment.added invalidate the cached entries
- [ ] Setup instructions shown in the admin integration screen

## Tests

Unit: signature check; integration: invalidation.

issues.title: Use my active Armature theme

## Tests

Integration against the stub; Playwright: enable follow and see the theme applied.

issues.title: Backup and restore
issues.body:
## User story

As an operator, I want documented backup and restore so that no data is lost.

## Decision

The first version is an operator backup, not an in-app export: one command takes a consistent database dump plus a copy of every object in storage, and one command restores it. Two install paths are covered, Docker Compose and the Helm chart. Scheduled backups with retention are out of scope for now; a site-wide export from the UI would be a separate issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Docker Compose**: a backup command writes one archive (database dump, object storage contents, the Stator version it was taken with); a restore command brings an empty stack back from it and refuses an archive from a newer version.
- [ ] **Helm chart**: CloudNativePG backups to object storage and the attachment bucket configured through chart values, with a documented restore into a fresh release.
- [ ] `docs/backup-and-restore.md` covers both paths, what is and is not in a backup (for example secrets and Keycloak), and how to check a restore.
- [ ] **Restore tested in CI**: fill a stack with pages, versions, attachments, comments and permissions, back it up, wipe it, restore it, and check everything is back and readable through the API, including the row level security on restored rows.

## Tests

Unit tests for the archive and its refusals, a chart test for the jobs, an integration test that every PL/pgSQL function pins its search_path (a dump restores with an empty one), and the backup round trip as a layer of its own against the compose stack.

issues.title: Read your own writes when a replica serves reads
issues.body:
## User story

As a user, I want to see my own change right after I make it, so that a save never seems to be lost because the next read hit a replica that hasn't caught up yet.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Writes return their LSN (the db cluster already does this). After a write, the API pins that session's reads to the primary until the replica has replayed that position, as Armature does with its Valkey-backed tracker (`ARMATURE_READ_YOUR_WRITES_TTL`).
- [ ] Tracked per session in Valkey, with a TTL from `STATOR_READ_YOUR_WRITES_TTL`.
- [ ] Handlers stop discarding the write position.
- [ ] The integration suite runs with the replica configured again (`mk/stack.mk` currently leaves it out of the suite's environment for this reason).

## Tests

Integration: write then immediately read through the API with the replica configured, repeated enough times to catch lag. The theme tests that failed with the replica pass.

issues.title: Kubernetes deployment with CloudNativePG read and write services
issues.body:
## User story

As an operator running Stator on Kubernetes, I want a CloudNativePG cluster whose write service takes all writes and whose read service takes the reads, so that read traffic scales across replicas and the primary stays free for writes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Helm chart `deploy/charts/stator`, modelled on Armature's `deploy/charts/armature`:
  - `cnpg.enabled` renders a `postgresql.cnpg.io/v1` Cluster (instances, storage, resources and backup passed through from `cnpg.spec`), as in Armature's `cnpg-cluster.yaml`
  - the api, worker, migrate and seed deployments and jobs, plus a roles job for `stator_app` / `stator_admin`
  - an ingress, a ServiceMonitor, and Valkey / S3 settings
- [ ] Write path: `STATOR_DB_PRIMARY_URL` points at `<cluster>-rw`. Migrations and admin work use it too.
- [ ] Read path: `STATOR_DB_REPLICA_URLS` points at `<cluster>-ro` when `cnpg.readReplicas` is on and `instances > 1`, otherwise it is empty and reads go to `-rw`. Same rules as Armature's `_helpers.tpl`.
- [ ] Reads stay correct behind a load-balanced `-ro` service, because one connection can land on any replica:
  - replica lag is sampled per connection and bounded (`STATOR_DB_MAX_REPLICA_LAG`, `STATOR_DB_REPLICA_LAG_SAMPLES`, as in Armature); a lagging replica falls back to the primary
  - read-your-writes (#120) checks `pg_last_wal_replay_lsn()` on the connection it actually got, not on the service
- [ ] Separate pool sizes for the write and read pools (`STATOR_DB_PRIMARY_MAX_CONNS`, `STATOR_DB_REPLICA_MAX_CONNS`), plus Prometheus metrics per pool (queries, wait time, fallbacks to primary).
- [ ] Guard: `cnpg.enabled` and a bundled Postgres can't both be on; the chart fails with a sentence saying which to turn off.
- [ ] `docs/architecture.md` and a deployment section in the README describe the write and read services.

## Tests

- Go unit tests for read routing: replica chosen, lag fallback, LSN pinning per connection.
- Integration against the compose primary and replica: pause replay on the replica (`pg_wal_replay_pause()`) and show that reads fall back to the primary and still see the last write.
- `helm lint` and `helm template` with cnpg on and off, with `instances: 1` and `instances: 3`, checked by a shell test in `run-tests.sh` (Helm runs in a container).

issues.title: Map identity provider groups to org roles
issues.body:
## User story

As an org admin, I want groups from our identity provider to grant roles in Stator, so that access follows what we already manage centrally.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On the SSO settings page, admins map IdP group names (values of the groups claim) to org roles (member, admin). Several groups can map to the same role.
- [ ] On every SSO sign-in, the person's role follows the mapping; the highest mapped role wins. When a group disappears, the role it granted goes too, but never below member while they are still a member.
- [ ] A mapped group counts as the admin's approval given in advance: a first sign-in by someone in a mapped group joins directly with that role. Everyone else still waits for approval (#5).
- [ ] Roles an admin set by hand for people outside any mapped group are left alone. The UI shows which roles come from the IdP.
- [ ] The org owner is never demoted by a mapping.
- [ ] Every role change the mapping makes is recorded for the audit log.

## Tests

- Unit tests for resolving the mapping.
- Integration through Keycloak: alice (`stator-administrators`) becomes admin once that group is mapped, and loses it when the group is removed in Keycloak.
- A Playwright case for the mapping UI.

issues.title: Throwaway organisations for end-to-end test isolation
issues.body:
## User story

As a developer, I want every end-to-end spec file to run in its own throwaway organisation, so that specs run in parallel without sharing the `demo` org's data.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test-only endpoint, enabled only when `STATOR_TEST_ENDPOINTS=1` (set in compose for the suite, never by the Helm chart), creates an org with a unique slug. Alice (admin) and bob (member) are pre-approved in it, and its SSO provider points at the compose Keycloak realm.
- [ ] A matching endpoint deletes that org and all its data, including S3 objects.
- [ ] Sign-in works for any such slug.
- [ ] `e2e/fixtures/org.ts` `freshOrg` uses these endpoints. The theme specs move from the shared `demo` org to their own org and run in parallel again.
- [ ] The endpoints return 404 when the setting is off. An integration test proves it.

## Tests

- Integration: create, use and delete an org, and the 404 when disabled.
- The theme specs run in parallel.

issues.title: Text keeps a readable measure while wide blocks use the window
issues.body:
## User story

As a reader on a wide screen, I want a page to use the window's width where its content needs it, so that wide content gets room while text stays comfortable to read.

## Background

A page's content is held to one column, `max-w-3xl` (48rem; the app's root font size is 14px, so 672px), in the reader and the editor. The per-page "Full" width in Appearance lifts the limit for one page at a time.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Text keeps a comfortable measure: paragraphs, headings, lists, quotes and the title stay within a readable line length (about 80 to 90 characters, named in `web/src/config.ts`), centred in the content area.
- [ ] Wide blocks use the content area's width, up to a named maximum: tables, charts from tables, diagrams, math blocks, images, galleries, columns, embeds and link cards, roadmaps, calendars, Armature charts and issue lists, and code blocks.
- [ ] The layout is the same in the reader, the editor, a version and the comparison in history, and the public reading view.
- [ ] The editor's toolbar, block handles, slash menu and remote carets still line up with the content.
- [ ] Narrow screens are unchanged, and nothing scrolls sideways on a phone.
- [ ] "Full" width also widens text to the content area.

## Tests

vitest where logic is involved, and Playwright checks on a wide window that text keeps its measure while a table and a diagram reach the wider width, in the reader and the editor, plus a phone check that nothing scrolls sideways.

issues.title: An example space that explains Stator
issues.body:
## User story

As an administrator, I want a button that creates an example space explaining Stator, so that a new team learns how to use it, and sees what pages can hold, from Stator itself.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Administrators find a "Create the example space" action (on the spaces overview and in organization settings). It creates a space with a fixed key and name, or says so and links to it if it already exists.
- [ ] The space's pages explain Stator: spaces and pages, the page tree and folders, drafts, publishing and history, editing together, comments and reactions, labels, watching and notifications, search, permissions, guests, anonymous spaces and public links, templates, attachments and previews, Armature integration, tokens and the MCP tools.
- [ ] A rich text showcase shows every block and mark the editor offers, each with a short note on how to insert it (slash menu, toolbar or shortcut): headings, lists and task lists, tables and charts from tables, panels, expands, columns, code, math, diagrams, decisions, link cards and embeds, excerpts and includes, page properties and reports, task reports, calendars, files blocks, template buttons, contributors, Armature blocks, dates, status, emoji and mentions.
- [ ] Blocks that need data (Armature, calendars, reports) show working examples where the site can provide them, and a sentence where it cannot.
- [ ] The content is written in English and German, following the person's language when the space is made.
- [ ] A test fails when the editor gains a block that the showcase does not show.
- [ ] Creating the space is audited; nobody but administrators may do it, and the database refuses it too.

## Tests

Unit tests for the content (every allowlisted node appears, the documents pass the allowlist), integration tests against the compose stack for creating it once and refusing members, and a Playwright test that an administrator creates it and reads the showcase.

issues.title: Let somebody edit one page without editing the whole space
issues.body:
## User story

As a space administrator, I want to let somebody edit one page and the pages below it without giving them Add pages in the whole space, so that a reader of the space can look after the pages that are theirs.

## Today

Editing a page needs the space's Add pages right. A page's restriction lists only narrow what the space allows, and a page must pass the lists of every page above it, so there is no way to open a single page or branch to an editor. Putting somebody who may only view the space on a page's "Who can edit" list changes nothing, and the dialog does not say so.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The restrictions dialog has a third list, "Also allowed to edit", of people and groups who may edit the page and the pages below it although the space does not let them add pages. The view and edit lists keep narrowing as before.
- [ ] Somebody on that list must still be able to view the page; the list never lets anybody past a view list or into a space they cannot view.
- [ ] The grant covers editing (drafts, publishing, live saves, files, restrictions as editors may change them today), not adding new pages, unless it is decided otherwise and recorded.
- [ ] The edit rule in the database (`perm_page_editable` and whatever else decides editing) takes the grant into account, and the guards are proven through SQL as the app role.
- [ ] The access report on a page names the grant when it decides an answer.
- [ ] Guests, tokens limited to spaces, copying a space's permissions and copying pages handle the new grant consistently, and the choices are recorded in docs/decisions.md.
- [ ] The restrictions dialog marks people and groups on the "Who can edit" list who still cannot edit, and says what to do (add them to "Also allowed to edit", or give them Add pages in the space).
- [ ] Changing the list is audited like other restriction changes.

## Tests

Unit tests for the logic, integration tests against the compose stack including the SQL guards, and a Playwright test: an administrator lets bob, who may only view the space, edit one page; bob edits and publishes it and cannot edit its sibling; the warning shows for somebody on the edit list who cannot edit.

issues.title: Give the example showcase page a cover picture
issues.body:
## User story

As an administrator trying the example space, I want the "Every block a page can hold" page to show a cover picture, so that I see what a cover looks like and that pages can have one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The example space gives the showcase page a cover picture, made with the space like its other pictures, with a focus point set.
- [ ] The showcase says in a sentence, in English and German, what the cover is and where it is set (the page menu, Appearance).
- [ ] Without file storage, the page has no cover and says so in a sentence, as the other file examples do.

## Tests

Unit test that the showcase asks for a cover; the integration test of the example space finds the cover on the page; the browser test sees it.

issues.title: Draw sketches in a page with an Excalidraw block
issues.body:
## User story

As an author, I want to draw a sketch right in a page, with shapes, arrows, text and freehand lines, so that a quick architecture drawing or whiteboard idea lives with the page instead of in a picture nobody can change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A **Sketch** block from the slash menu opens a drawing canvas built on Excalidraw (MIT), loaded only when a sketch is opened, from the app's own build with no third-party host.
- [ ] The drawing is stored in the page as its scene (JSON) within a size limit, so versions, history comparison, copy, templates and editing together carry it like any other block.
- [ ] Readers see it drawn as SVG in the read view, includes, public and link views and the PDF print, and can open it larger; only editors change it.
- [ ] Pictures used in a sketch are the page's own files, so permissions and copies hold.
- [ ] Markdown export writes the sketch so that import brings it back; the example space showcase shows one, in English and German, with how to insert it.
- [ ] The block passes axe in light and dark, works by keyboard as far as the canvas allows, and fits a phone.

## Tests

Unit tests for the scene's validation and size limit, integration tests that the server keeps only valid scenes and that copy and Markdown round trip them, and a Playwright test that draws a box with text, publishes, and sees it in the read view and in history.

issues.title: Review pages before they publish, and confirm reading them
issues.body:
## User story

As a space administrator, I want pages to be reviewed before they are published, and readers to confirm they have read important pages, so that procedures and policies go out checked and we know who has seen them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A space, or a branch of its pages, can require a review: publishing a draft then asks one or more named reviewers (people or groups) instead of going out at once.
- [ ] Reviewers are notified, see the draft and its comparison with the published version, and approve or ask for changes with a comment; the draft goes out when the required approvals are in, as its author.
- [ ] The page shows that a review is pending and who decided what; history records who approved each version.
- [ ] Administrators can skip a review with a reason, which is audited.
- [ ] A page can ask its readers to confirm they have read it; the page lists who has and has not, and a new version can ask again.
- [ ] Guards hold in the database: only named reviewers approve, nobody approves their own draft, a page under review is not published around it.
- [ ] Live pages, scheduled publishing and blog posts behave consistently with reviews, and the choices are recorded.

## Tests

Unit tests for the review rules, integration tests including the SQL guards, and a Playwright test: alice requires a review, bob's draft waits, alice approves, the page goes out, and carol confirms she read it.

issues.title: Renew the example space when a newer one ships
issues.body:
## User story

As an administrator, I want to know when Stator ships a newer example space and renew ours with one click, so that the guides and the showcase keep describing what Stator can do today.

## Today

The example space is made once (#288, #306). When later releases add features (live pages, PDF and Word export, space import, the sketch block), an existing example space keeps its old pages and never mentions them; the only way to a current one is to delete it and make it again.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The example's content carries a version that changes whenever its pages change; the example space records the version it was made from.
- [ ] Administrators see, on the spaces overview, in the example space and in its settings page, that a newer example is available, with a short list of what is new (written with the content, in English and German).
- [ ] **Renew** replaces the example space's guide pages, showcase and their files with the current ones, through the worker job as making it does, in the language it was made in or one the administrator picks. The space keeps its key, and what people added (their own pages, comments, labels, stars and watches on pages that still exist) is kept or reported; record the choice.
- [ ] Pages people changed since the example was made are not overwritten silently: they are kept, renamed or listed in a report, as decided and recorded.
- [ ] Renewing is audited, only administrators may do it, and the database refuses it too.

## Tests

Unit tests for the version and the what-is-new list (a test fails when the content changes without a new version), integration tests for renewing an older example including the SQL guards and kept additions, and a Playwright test: an administrator sees that a newer example is available, renews it, and reads a new guide.

issues.title: Brand exports with the organization's logo, name and colours
issues.body:
## User story

As an organization administrator, I want our exports to carry our brand, so that a PDF, Word document or offline HTML copy of a page looks like it comes from us.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Organization settings gain a **logo** (an uploaded picture, with size and type limits) shown in the app's header, and an optional footer line (for example a classification or a contact), in English and German.
- [ ] PDF export (#86) prints the logo and the organization's name in its header, the footer line in its footer, and uses the organization's theme colours for headings, links and panels.
- [ ] Word export (#87) puts the logo and name in the document header, the footer line in its footer, and the theme's colours in its heading and link styles.
- [ ] The HTML export of a space (#88) carries the logo, the name and the theme's colours in its stylesheet.
- [ ] Public and link exports carry the same brand; a page without an organization logo falls back to the name alone.
- [ ] Only organization administrators change the brand; the change is audited and the database refuses it from anyone else.

## Tests

Unit tests for the Word header and styles and the HTML stylesheet, integration tests that each export carries the logo and footer line and that members cannot change them (also through SQL), and a Playwright test: an administrator uploads a logo and footer line, exports a page as PDF and Word, and finds both in the files.

issues.title: Take a task's link to the task on its page
issues.body:
## User story

As somebody with tasks on many pages, I want a task's link to take me to that task on its page, so that I do not have to search a long page for it.

## Today

**My tasks**, the task report block and the notification that a task was assigned all link to the page itself, so the page opens at its top. Each task in the read view already carries its id (`data-task-id`), but no link points at it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A task's link from **My tasks**, the task report, the assignment notification (in the app and in its email) and the task's MCP tool result carries the task's id, for example `/s/KEY/p/ID/slug#task-<id>`.
- [ ] Opening such a link scrolls the task into view once the page has drawn, below the sticky header, and marks it briefly so the eye finds it; the mark respects reduced motion.
- [ ] It works when the task sits inside a collapsed expand (which opens), in columns, a panel or a table cell, and in an included page's copy of it is not chosen over the page's own.
- [ ] If the task is gone from the published page (deleted, or only in a draft), the page opens at its top with a short note that says so.
- [ ] Focus moves to the task for keyboard and screen reader users.

## Tests

Unit tests for building and reading the anchor, and a Playwright test: bob is assigned a task far down a long page and inside a collapsed expand, follows it from My tasks and from his notification, and lands on it.

issues.title: A suite demo space filled with the documentation of Stator, Armature and Exciter
issues.body:
## User story

As someone trying Stator together with Armature and Exciter, I want a demo whose pages are the suite's own documentation, so that I see the three tools working on real, linked content rather than invented examples.

Part of one suite demo: Armature holds the issues (Cloudster1/Armature#300), Stator the documentation and Exciter the requirements (Cloudster1/Exciter#270), and Exciter traces between them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Adding it:** an administrator adds the suite demo once, beside the example space, and `make seed` adds it too. It is refused when one of its keys is taken.
- [ ] **Spaces:** three spaces, `ARM`, `EXC` and `STA`, each hold the README, CONTRIBUTING, CHANGELOG and every Markdown file under `docs/` of their tool's repository, in its folder tree. Images become attachments.
- [ ] **Decisions:** `docs/decisions.md` becomes a page with one child page per top-level section, so no page is too long to read or edit.
- [ ] **Links between docs:** links between docs become page links, also across tools (a GitHub link from Exciter's docs to Armature's `docs/integration.md` opens that page in `ARM`). Links to source files point at GitHub, at the snapshot's commit.
- [ ] **Issue references:** `#261` in Exciter's docs and `Cloudster1/Armature#213` anywhere become issue chips (`EXC-261`, `ARM-213`). They resolve once Armature has its suite demo, and publishing puts the page links on those issues.
- [ ] **Labels for partners:** every page carries a label naming its source file (for example `demo-exc-docs-api-contract-m13`), so Exciter finds it through `GET /labels/{name}/pages`.
- [ ] **Snapshot:** the content comes from a snapshot in the repository, so adding the demo needs no network. `make demo-snapshot` refreshes it from the three repositories and records the date and commit of each.

## Tests

- Go unit: link and reference rewriting (relative, cross-tool, source files, `#N` and `owner/repo#N`); splitting the decisions; label names.
- Integration: add the demo; a second add and a taken key are refused; the page trees match the snapshot; a cross-space page link and an issue chip are present.
- vitest: the control that adds the demo.
- Playwright: add the demo, open a decisions page and a page with a chip, with the accessibility check.

## Implementation

- Follows `backend/internal/example`: embedded content, a worker job that builds through the services as a person would, and `versions.json` for renewal.
- The folder import of `internal/mdio`.
- A decision in `docs/decisions.md`: why a snapshot and not git sync.

## Depends on

- Nothing to build. The chips resolve with Cloudster1/Armature#300.
